chunks: Which snatched away men as though they were palm trees pulled out by the roots.

key_terms.أَعْجَازُ: Trunks or stems of palm trees
key_terms.مُنْقَعِرٍ: Uprooted or pulled out by the roots

ai.seo_question: How does the Quran describe the manner of death or soul extraction?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Qamar is often interpreted as describing the violent and abrupt extraction of souls at the moment of death or on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the helplessness of the human spirit against divine command. The simile of 'uprooted palm trunks' (a'jaz nakhl munqir) underscores the suddenness and total detachment of the soul from the body, a concept frequently linked to the Hadith of the Angel of Death's forceful grip. This imagery serves as a reminder of the fragility of worldly life and the inevitability of returning to the Creator.
